thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: abnormal spike of 5xx/resets from ingress-proxy-nlb in euc1 (AZ-b). PagerDuty: PD-3345. Auto-escalation triggered.

sarah: just got paged — seeing elevated 502/504s in dashboard. Affects routes for customer-facing API and webhooks.

raj: ACK — I'm on call. starting triage. TL;DR: ~12-18% error rate across euc1, errors are connection resets (ECONNRESET) at NLB -> envoy.

infra-bot: metrics snapshot: NLB connection resets = 4.5k/min, 5xx rate +1500% in last 5m. Backend target healthy_count dropping in AZ-b.

maria: are these new Envoy config changes deployed? any recent ingress-chart rollouts?

kevin: no deploys in the last 24h. Chart change would show in deploy bot — none. Suspect underlying network/AZ issue.

raj: confirmed no recent ingress-chart changes. logs show repeated TLS handshake failures + connection reset from NLB side. sample:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:02Z] envoy upstream reset: connection failure, remote_reset, tls_handshake_error
[...snip...]
```

ops-lead: impact assessment: primary API paths ~15% error, realtime webhooks delayed or retried. A few pro customers in EU reporting elevated latency. set incident severity = P1.

raj: mitigation plan (short): 1) remove targets in AZ-b from target-group, 2) shift traffic weight to euc2 by increasing route weight and lowering DNS TTL temporarily, 3) enable per-route retries in Envoy and increase upstream timeouts. attempting step 1 now.

kevin: I'll run target-group update. CLI snippet:
```
# remove instances in AZ-b from target group
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn tg-abc123 --targets Id=i-0aa1bb2cc3dd4
# or set weight=0 for NLB route if using weighted target groups
```

cloud-support: we opened a ticket with cloud provider (case 987654). they report possible packet drops in euc1 AZ-b. asking for flow logs and target health.

infra-bot: executed change: 3 targets deregistered from AZ-b at 10:18Z. health_count stable for remaining targets. NLB resets dropped to ~900/min after removal.

maria: enabling retries + timeout bump on envoy now. small config:
```
route:
  retry_policy:
    retry_on: 5xx,connect-failure
    num_retries: 3
  timeout: 30s
```

raj: retries live at 10:22Z. observing error rate drop to 6%. some upstream 504s persist where connections timed out.

kevin: also started scaling euc2 target pools + increased ephemeral capacity to absorb traffic. DNS TTL lowered to 30s so CloudFront/clients will favor euc2 sooner.

cloud-support: provider update: they confirm partial NIC hardware degradation in AZ-b affecting connections to LB. they propose moving affected NLB nodes to healthy hosts — ETA 40-60m, or customer can failover to other AZs.

ops-lead: do not wait for provider fix if customer impact persists. continue traffic shift and consider full AZ-b circuit breaker: mark AZ-b as drained in routing policy for the cluster.

raj: implemented AZ-b circuit breaker in routing: set az_awareness_disable = true for target-routing group, and updated local balancer to avoid AZ-b IP ranges.

sarah: customer comms: drafting status update. will send to impacted customers: summary, mitigation steps, ETA.

kevin: quick note — we saw NLB connection reset spikes correlate with heavy TCP connection churn from one internal autoscaling job in AZ-b. paused that job as low-risk rollback.

infra-bot: post-mitigation metrics: 5xx rate back to baseline in euc1 after full AZ-b drain + envoys changes. residual error rate ~0.4%.

cloud-support: provider finished remediation at 11:05Z, moved NLB instances off degraded hosts. recommended follow-ups: run connection soak, check NIC error counters.

raj: closing mitigation loop. next steps (action items):
- add automated AZ draining policy when per-AZ healthy_count < threshold (maria)
- lower DNS TTL for ingress LB in config (kevin)
- add alert for NLB connection resets with AZ granularity (sarah)
- run post-incident load test to validate failover (infra-team)
- contact affected customers with RCA once postmortem done (ops-lead)

ops-lead: handoff: raj done for now, on-call shift ends. kevin will take follow-up during his shift starting 11:30Z. @kevin please ack.

kevin: ACK — I'll monitor for 2h and start postmortem draft.

sarah: posted customer update v1 to status.redwood.ai/incidents/PD-3345 and added note to support queue. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident PD-3345 status: mitigated -> monitoring. responders: raj, kevin, maria, sarah. Escalation closed.

maria: quick doc note for postmortem: consider exposing per-AZ LB metrics in Console + runbook for cross-AZ failover.

ops-lead: great work team — keep follow-ups in the postmortem thread. thanks. :heart:
